CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on medication efficacy and quality of life improvements.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing a blend of optimism and ongoing challenges with his mental health regimen. He reports that the continuation of trazodone at 100 mg nightly has maintained its effectiveness in improving his sleep initiation and reducing nocturnal awakenings. However, he notes that while he sleeps longer, he still feels somewhat unrested upon waking, suggesting possible residual sleep fragmentation.
Mr. Smith continues to experience episodes of anxiety, particularly during demanding work periods, despite utilizing lorazepam 1 mg as needed. He reports that while this medication provides temporary relief, it does not fully alleviate his anxiety symptoms. He expresses interest in exploring alternative therapies, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) group sessions, to enhance his coping mechanisms.
His tension-type headaches have persisted, occurring approximately twice a week with an intensity rating fluctuating between 4 to 6 out of 10. He has been adhering to the ibuprofen regimen of 600 mg as needed, which offers moderate relief; however, he notes an increase in headache frequency correlating with recent project deadlines and heightened workplace stress. His headache diary continues to be a valuable tool, although he reports difficulty identifying specific triggers.
Mr. Smiths persistent fatigue remains a significant concern, although he feels that the bupropion at 150 mg daily is contributing positively to his overall energy levels and mood. He reports increased engagement in physical activities, including yoga and brisk walking, which he notes have positively impacted his mental health. However, he admits to occasional lapses in motivation, particularly during high-stress work periods.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 10. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to participate in physical activities that he finds beneficial for his mental health. He has maintained a balanced diet and remains vigilant about his caffeine intake, reporting a reduction. He actively engages in mindfulness and meditation practices but acknowledges that work-related stressors continue to challenge his overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety remains a concern; sleep quality is improved but not optimal; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has increased; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue, though improved; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears fatigued; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Consider increasing lorazepam frequency for acute anxiety management if symptoms persist, with a plan to reassess in one month. Discuss potential referral for group therapy. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime, monitoring for side effects and sleep quality. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; recommend maintaining ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. If headaches increase in frequency or intensity, consider referral to a neurologist for further evaluation. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage consistent physical activity and stress management techniques.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-12-12 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to continue documenting his symptoms and medication responses to facilitate ongoing management.
